calls.reasoning: The quarter ended Sep 30 and the report is due Oct 29. Operating income guidance is $22.5-26.5B, and Amazon usually beats the top of its guide (Q2: $27.5B against a $20-24B guide). That points to about $27-28B of operating income. With about 20% tax and 10.9B diluted shares, GAAP EPS comes to about $2.00-2.10. Consensus is $1.96-2.03. Big GAAP jumps in Q1 and Q2 2026 came from Anthropic remeasurements tied to priced primary rounds. None of the three runs found such a round for Q3: Amazon's $5B Series H exercise was at the same price, and the IPO is in Q4. So the base case has no big gain. Upside tail: a note conversion that moves gains from OCI into income, or an observable price change. Smaller downside tail: a write-down if the reported $852B tender is treated as an observable price. Polymarket: a thin market (about $3k volume) on GAAP EPS beating about $2.00 trades near 62%. It is consistent with this median but too thin to anchor on.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the core: the guidance, Q2 actuals, consensus of $1.96-2.03, and no priced Anthropic primary round in Q3. Their medians ($2.04-2.08) differ only by judgment about how far Amazon beats its operating-income guide. I take about $27.5B, which gives a median near $2.06. Factual disputes I could not settle (no web access this run): (1) Run 3's August employee tender at $852B, which only Run 3 reported. Even if it is real, a tender for common shares is a weak observable price for Amazon's preferred stock, so I give the downside escape (below $0.995, which would need roughly a $14B pre-tax write-down) about 3%, below Run 3's 6%. (2) The Polymarket contract: Runs 1 and 2 report it, Run 3 found none. It is thin either way and not load-bearing. (3) Upside escape from note conversion or fair-valued commitments: about 8%, within the runs' 7-10% range. Run 1's upper tail is wider than this evidence supports, given that no Q3 trigger event was found.
